newsitem.title: USA: Campbell in deal on retiree medical costs.
newsitem.headline: Campbell in deal on retiree medical costs.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co. said Tuesday it reached a tentative $114.5 million settlement with a group of retired employees who sued the company after it cut their medical benefits in 1992.

Under the settlement, which must be approved by a federal court judge in Camden, N.J., where Campbell is based, the company will pay the money to help cover medical costs for the 12,000 retirees and their dependents, Campbell spokesman Kevin Lowery said.

Lowery said the court had ruled that Campbell had the right to cut the benefits but the case has remained open to consider whether Campbell had properly communicated the cuts to its retired employees.

"We went to the other side, and working together with them, we made a proposal that said we would be willing to put money into a fund that would essentially provide lifetime medical benefits," Lowery said.

The fund will provide managed-care coverage, including up to 80 percent of drug costs, through health maintenance organisations. Retirees who wished to continue in the federal Medicare programme also would receive prescription drug benefits and reimbursements for 80 percent of prescription costs.
The agreement includes a $3.5 million hardship fund for special cases, and provides reimbursement for certain costs borne by retirees since 1992, Lowery said.
U.S. District Court Judge Stanley Brotman set a hearing on the plan for Jan. 10.

Lowery said former employees eligible for the proposed settlement were notified of the deal by mail last week. The proposal does not affect Campbell employees who retired after the cut in benefits was announced.
Lowery also said the settlement, if approved, would not affect earnings Campbell because the costs had been already accounted for.
Campbell stock rose 37.5 cents to $81.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
